summary: Part II of PerfectoidQuotients: the structure theory of integral perfectoid rings beyond the parent's Layer 0 and the ordinary ind-syntomic André lemma, following Česnavičius–Scholze, Purity for flat cohomology, §§2.1 and 2.3. Q5 proves the multiplicative description of the tilt of any p-adically complete ring, the identifications A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^p ≅ A/ϖ^p, the torsion comparison A^♭[ϖ^♭] ≅ A[ϖ] and that fibre products of perfectoid rings along a surjection are perfectoid. Q6 proves the relative tilting equivalence with its completeness transfer, the tilting of valuation rings of arbitrary rank with their value groups and algebraically closed fraction fields, and that perfectoid rings are quotients of torsion-free ones (strengthened with compatible roots). Q7 defines ind-fppf and ind-syntomic ring maps and proves the commutative-algebra inputs (glueing of flatness, blowup algebras of regular pairs, fibrewise hypersurfaces). Q8 tilts continuous valuations and proves the integral approximation lemma and the valuative criterion for topological nilpotence. Q9 constructs André's root extension and proves the ind-syntomic André lemma and the semiperfectoid covers of p-Zariski rings. Q10 relates the regular towers of PerfectoidSpaces P7, constructs Bhatt–Scholze's prismatic perfectoid cover of a complete regular local ring, and proves Bhatt–Scholze's almost vanishing of Tor along finite subextensions of R⁺ (Remark 10.13) for perfect residue fields, with the general case reduced to a recorded gap. The general perfectoidization of integral algebras and almost purity along arbitrary ideals (Bhatt–Scholze §§8.2 and 10) are imported from PrismaticCohomology, Part I.

nodes.title: The tilt as an inverse limit along p-th powers
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. Let A be a ring that is classically p-adically complete and separated; if A is nonzero then p is not a unit of A. (1) Reduction modulo p induces a bijection of multiplicative monoids lim_{x ↦ x^p} A → A^♭ = lim_{x ↦ x^p} A/pA (Mathlib's PreTilt A p). Its inverse sends a = (a_n)_n to the sequence whose n-th term is lim_m (ã_{n+m})^{p^m} for arbitrary lifts ã_k ∈ A of a_k; its zeroth coordinate is Mathlib's multiplicative untilt a ↦ a^♯, so that the n-th coordinate is (a^{1/p^n})^♯, where a^{1/p^n} is the image of a under the inverse of the n-th power of Frobenius of the perfect ring A^♭. (2) If ϖ ∈ A divides p and A is classically ϖ-adically complete, reduction gives a ring isomorphism lim_{x ↦ x^p} A/pA → lim_{x ↦ x^p} A/ϖA, so A^♭ may be computed with ϖ in place of p. (3) For A nonzero, Fontaine's map θ : W(A^♭) → A is the unique ring map with θ([a]) = a^♯ for every a ∈ A^♭.
hypotheses: p prime; A commutative; classical completeness means A → lim_n A/p^nA is bijective.
In (2) ϖ need not be a nonzerodivisor and need not have p-power roots.
This is the statement for every p-adically complete ring; PerfectoidQuotients Q0 records the multiplicative isomorphism only for p-torsion-free integral perfectoid rings.
proofSteps: For x ∈ A with x ≡ y mod p one has x^{p^m} ≡ y^{p^m} mod p^{m+1}; hence for a compatible system (a_n) in A/p the limits lim_m (ã_{n+m})^{p^m} exist, do not depend on the lifts, and form a p-power compatible sequence in A (completeness and separatedness).

The two maps are mutually inverse and multiplicative; the zeroth coordinate of the inverse is PreTilt.untilt by mathlib:PreTilt.mk_untilt_eq_coeff_zero and mathlib:PreTilt.untilt_iterate_frobeniusEquiv_symm_pow.
For (2), the same congruence modulo ϖ (ϖ | p) shows that lim_{x ↦ x^p} A → lim_{x ↦ x^p} A/ϖA is bijective; composing with (1) gives the ring isomorphism.

For (3), θ([a]) = a^♯ is mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta_teichmuller; a ring map W(A^♭) → A is determined by its values on Teichmüller representatives, because both sides are p-adically complete and W(A^♭)/p^n is generated by Teichmüller lifts of p^n-th roots (mathlib:WittVector.eq_of_apply_teichmuller_eq applied to each A/p^n).
acceptance: For A = Z_p the bijection identifies Z_p^♭ = F_p with the p-power compatible sequences in Z_p, which are the constant sequences of Teichmüller roots of unity and 0.
For a perfect F_p-algebra A the map a ↦ a^♯ is the identity of A = A^♭.
For A = O_C with C complete algebraically closed, the element ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) of O_C^♭ has ε^♯ = 1 = 1^♯ with ε ≠ 1, so ♯ is not injective.

sources.match: States that for p-adically complete A reduction gives a multiplicative isomorphism from the p-power inverse limit of A to A^♭, defines ♯ as the projection, notes θ([a]) = a^♯ with a footnote proof, and that ϖ may replace p when ϖ | p and A is ϖ-adically complete.
The canonical maps from the p-power inverse limit of S to S^♭ and on to the Frobenius inverse limit of S/πS are isomorphisms of monoids, respectively rings, for S π-adically complete with π | p.

nodes.title: Tilts and A_inf of products and fibre products
nodes.statement: Fix a prime p. (1) For any family (A_i)_{i∈I} of classically p-adically complete rings, the product ∏_i A_i is p-adically complete and the projections induce ring isomorphisms (∏_i A_i)^♭ ≅ ∏_i A_i^♭ and A_inf(∏_i A_i) ≅ ∏_i A_inf(A_i), compatible with θ. (2) Let A → A' ← B be ring maps of classically p-adically complete rings and suppose A'[p^∞] = A'[p]. Then C = A ×_{A'} B is classically p-adically complete, p^{n+1}(A × B) ∩ C ⊆ p^n C for all n, and the induced maps C^♭ → A^♭ ×_{A'^♭} B^♭ and A_inf(C) → A_inf(A) ×_{A_inf(A')} A_inf(B) are ring isomorphisms compatible with θ.
hypotheses: Tilts are Mathlib's PreTilt and A_inf(A) = W(A^♭) with Mathlib's Witt vectors.
The bounded-torsion hypothesis on A' holds for every integral perfectoid A' (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, bounded p-torsion).
proofSteps: (1): (∏A_i)/p = ∏(A_i/p), and inverse limits and Witt vectors commute with products.

(2), completeness: if (a, b) = p^{n+1}(a_1, b_1) lies in C, the defect e = f(a_1) − g(b_1) is killed by p^{n+1}, hence by p, so (pa_1, pb_1) ∈ C and (a, b) ∈ p^nC. Thus the p-adic topology of C is the subspace topology from A × B; C is closed there because A' is separated, hence complete.

(2), tilt: by Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid, C^♭ is the p-power inverse limit of C as a monoid; inverse limits commute with fibre products, so the ring map C^♭ → A^♭ ×_{A'^♭} B^♭ is bijective. W(−) commutes with all limits of rings, giving the A_inf statement; compatibility with θ follows from θ([a]) = a^♯.
acceptance: For A' = 0 the fibre product is A × B and (2) reduces to (1) for two factors.
For A → A' = B the identity of B, C = A and the statement is the identity.
For A = B = O_C mapping to its residue field k̄, C = O_C ×_{k̄} O_C has tilt O_{C^♭} ×_{k̄} O_{C^♭}.

sources.locator: §2.1.1, p. 10; proof of Proposition 2.1.4, second paragraph, p. 12
sources.match: Notes that the tilt, W(−) and A_inf(−) commute with limits of rings, and in the proof of Proposition 2.1.4 that the fibre product C inherits p-adic completeness, so that its tilt and A_inf are the fibre products of those of the factors.

nodes.title: The tilt and the ring agree modulo ϖ^p
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid (PerfectoidSpaces P1.24) and let ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p be such that A is classically ϖ-adically complete. Choose ϖ^♭, p^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ and (p^♭)^♯ unit multiples of ϖ and p (they exist by PerfectoidSpaces P1.24). Then: (1) a ↦ a^♯ induces ring isomorphisms A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^pA^♭ ≅ A/ϖ^pA and A^♭/p^♭A^♭ ≅ A/pA; (2) consequently (ϖ^♭)^p divides p^♭ in A^♭, the ideals (ϖ^♭) and (p^♭) of A^♭ do not depend on the choices, and A^♭ is classically ϖ^♭-adically complete; (3) if A is nonzero, ker θ has a generator of the form ξ = p + [p^♭]x with θ(x) a unit of A, and p^♭ may be chosen so that p^♭ = ξ_0 is the zeroth Witt coordinate of this generator.
hypotheses: The integral perfectoid predicate is the single predicate of PerfectoidSpaces P1.24 used throughout; the zero ring is allowed.
Only ideals generated by ϖ^♭ and p^♭ are canonical; the elements are not.
proofSteps: The map A^♭ → A/ϖ^p, a ↦ a^♯ mod ϖ^p is a ring map: modulo ϖ^p it is the projection of lim_{Frob} A/ϖ (Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid (2)) to coordinate 1 (with coordinates numbered from 0) followed by the Frobenius A/ϖ → A/ϖ^p, which is bijective for integral perfectoid A (PerfectoidSpaces P1.24, BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i)).
It is surjective because Frobenius of A/p is surjective; its kernel is generated by (ϖ^♭)^p, following the proof of BMS1 Lemma 3.10(i). The same argument with p gives A^♭/p^♭ ≅ A/p.
(2) follows: p^♭ maps to 0 in A/ϖ^p, so it lies in ((ϖ^♭)^p); a ϖ^♭-adic Cauchy sequence stabilizes coordinatewise in lim_{Frob} A/ϖ, giving completeness.

(3): write p + [p^♭]x ∈ ker θ (possible as θ(p) ∈ (p^♭)^♯A); its first Witt coordinate is a unit (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, generator criterion), and choosing θ(x) a unit allows replacing p^♭ by ξ_0 through Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid.
acceptance: For A = O_C and ϖ = p^{1/p}: O_C^♭/((p^♭)^{1/p})^p ≅ O_C/p.
For a perfect F_p-algebra A, p^♭ = 0 is allowed and A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^p = A/ϖ^p is the identity.
For A the p-adic completion of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}], ϖ = p^{1/p} and t = p^♭, A^♭ is the t-adic completion of F_p[t^{1/p^∞}] and A^♭/t ≅ A/p ≅ F_p[t^{1/p^∞}]/(t).

sources.locator: §2.1.2, paragraphs after Definition (i)–(ii) and equation (2.1.2.2), pp. 10–11
sources.match: Recalls from BMS that unit multiples of ϖ and p have compatible p-power roots, shows that ker θ has a generator p + [p^♭]x with p^♭ = ξ_0 after adjustment, and that a ↦ a^♯ gives the isomorphisms A^♭/(ϖ^♭)^p ≅ A/ϖ^p and A^♭/p^♭ ≅ A/p, whence (ϖ^♭)^p | p^♭ and ϖ^♭-adic completeness of A^♭.

sources.match: Unit multiples of π and p admit compatible p-power roots, and for perfectoid S the map induced by ♯ identifies S^♭ modulo the corresponding element with S modulo π^p.

nodes.title: Torsion of a perfectoid ring and of its tilt
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid, ξ a generator of ker(θ : A_inf(A) → A) and p^♭ = ξ_0 as in Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms. (1) The A_inf(A)-module M = {(x, y) ∈ A_inf(A)² : ξx = py} / {(pz, ξz) : z ∈ A_inf(A)} maps isomorphically onto A^♭[p^♭] by (x, y) ↦ x mod p and onto A[p] by (x, y) ↦ y mod ξ; so A^♭[p^♭] ≅ A[p] as A_inf(A)-modules. (2) For ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p and A classically ϖ-adically complete, and ϖ^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ, there is an A_inf(A)-module isomorphism A^♭[ϖ^♭] ≅ A[ϖ]; in particular A^♭ is ϖ^♭-torsion-free if and only if A is ϖ-torsion-free. (3) If ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯ and ϖ^{1/p^n} = ((ϖ^♭)^{1/p^n})^♯, then A[ϖ] is killed by every ϖ^{1/p^n}, and A[ϖ^{1/p^n}] = A[ϖ] = A[ϖ^∞] for all n ≥ 0.
hypotheses: p and ξ are nonzerodivisors of A_inf(A): p because A^♭ is perfect, ξ by PerfectoidQuotients Q0 (generator criterion).
A[x] denotes the x-torsion submodule and A[x^∞] the x-power torsion.
proofSteps: (1): M is Tor_1^{A_inf(A)}(A_inf(A)/p, A_inf(A)/ξ), computed from the two Koszul resolutions: it is (A_inf/ξ)[p] = A[p] and (A_inf/p)[ξ] = A^♭[ξ_0] because ξ ≡ [ξ_0] mod p.

(2): the isomorphism of (1) is A_inf-linear; [ϖ^♭] acts on A[p] through θ([ϖ^♭]) = (ϖ^♭)^♯ and on A^♭[p^♭] through ϖ^♭. Since ϖ | p and (ϖ^♭)^p | p^♭ (Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms), A[ϖ] ⊆ A[p] and A^♭[ϖ^♭] ⊆ A^♭[p^♭] are the kernels of [ϖ^♭] on the two sides, which therefore correspond.

(3): apply (2) to ϖ^{1/p^n}, which also satisfies (ϖ^{1/p^n})^p | p, and use that in the perfect ring A^♭ the ϖ^♭-torsion and (ϖ^♭)^{1/p^n}-torsion and (ϖ^♭)-power torsion coincide; naturality of (2) identifies the inclusions.
acceptance: For A = O_C both sides of (1) are zero.
For A perfect of characteristic p, ξ = p, p^♭ = 0, and (1) says A[0] = A ≅ A[p] = A.
For A = O_C × F̄_p and ϖ = (p^{1/p}, 0), A[ϖ] = 0 × F̄_p and A^♭[ϖ^♭] = 0 × F̄_p, matching (2).

sources.match: Defines the A_inf-module of pairs (x, y) with ξx = py modulo (pz, ξz), identifies it with A^♭⟨p^♭⟩ and A⟨p⟩, deduces A^♭⟨ϖ^♭⟩ ≅ A⟨ϖ⟩ and the equalities A⟨ϖ^{1/p^∞}⟩ = A⟨ϖ⟩ = A⟨ϖ^∞⟩.

nodes.title: A_inf of a surjection of perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: Let f : A ↠ A' be a surjective map of integral perfectoid rings and ξ_A a generator of ker θ_A. Then A_inf(f) : A_inf(A) → A_inf(A') is surjective, ker(A_inf(f))/ξ_A·ker(A_inf(f)) ≅ ker f, A_inf(f) maps ker θ_A onto ker θ_{A'}, and the induced maps A_inf(A) → A_inf(A') ×_{A'} A and [p^♭]A_inf(A) → [p^♭]A_inf(A') ×_{pA'} pA are surjective.
hypotheses: Both rings are p-adically complete by the integral perfectoid predicate.
p^♭ is chosen for A as in Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms; its image serves for A'.
proofSteps: Surjectivity of A_inf(f) may be checked modulo p and then modulo p^♭ by completeness; there it is the surjection A^♭/p^♭ ≅ A/p → A'/p ≅ A'^♭/p^♭ (Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms).

ξ_A maps to a generator of ker θ_{A'} (PerfectoidQuotients Q0); the snake lemma for multiplication by ξ_A on 0 → ker A_inf(f) → A_inf(A) → A_inf(A') → 0 gives ker(A_inf(f))/ξ_A ≅ ker f and surjectivity on kernels of θ.

The first displayed surjection follows from surjectivity on kernels of θ and surjectivity of θ_A; the second follows by applying the first to the quotients by p-power torsion (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, torsion-free quotient).
acceptance: For A = A' and f the identity, every assertion is trivial.
For A = O_C and A' = O_C/(p^{1/p^∞}) = k̄, A_inf(O_C) = W(O_{C^♭}) → W(k̄) is surjective with kernel W(m_{C^♭}) and ker θ maps onto ker(θ_{k̄}) = (p).

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.4, first part, equation (2.1.4.1), and its proof, first paragraph, pp. 12–13
sources.match: States and proves that A_inf of a surjection of perfectoid rings is surjective, surjective on kernels of θ, and induces the two displayed surjections onto fibre products.

nodes.title: Fibre products of perfectoid rings
nodes.statement: Let f : A ↠ A' be a surjective map of integral perfectoid rings and g : B → A' any map from an integral perfectoid ring B. Then C = A ×_{A'} B is integral perfectoid, and the projections induce an isomorphism C^♭ ≅ A^♭ ×_{A'^♭} B^♭.
hypotheses: Surjectivity of f is used to produce a common generator of the kernels of θ; no flatness or torsion-freeness is assumed.
proofSteps: By Q5/tilt-of-limits (with A'[p^∞] = A'[p], PerfectoidQuotients Q0) C is p-adically complete, C^♭ is the fibre product of tilts and A_inf(C) = A_inf(A) ×_{A_inf(A')} A_inf(B).
By Q5/ainf-of-perfectoid-surjections there is ξ = p + [p^♭]x ∈ A_inf(C) mapping to generators of ker θ for A, A' and B.

The snake lemma gives A_inf(C)/(ξ) ≅ C; with ϖ the image of (p^♭)^{1/p} (up to a unit) this exhibits C as integral perfectoid (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, principal kernel criterion; PrismaticCohomology PR.0, perfect prisms and perfectoid rings).
acceptance: For A' = 0 this recovers integral perfectoidness of A × B (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, products).
O_C ×_{k̄} O_C, glued along the residue field, is integral perfectoid with tilt O_{C^♭} ×_{k̄} O_{C^♭}.
The decomposition A ≅ Ā ×_{(Ā/ϖ)_red} (A/ϖ)_red of PerfectoidQuotients Q0 is an instance, with A replaced by Ā and B = (A/ϖ)_red.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.4, second part, and its proof, second paragraph, pp. 12–13
sources.match: States that A ×_{A'} B is perfectoid with tilt the fibre product of tilts for a surjection A ↠ A' and any map B → A' of perfectoids, proved by completeness of C, a common generator p + [p^♭]x and the snake lemma.

nodes.title: Glueing a perfectoid ring with a perfect algebra
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid and ϖ ∈ A with ϖ | p such that A is classically ϖ-adically complete. For every perfect F_p-algebra B and every ring map B → (A/ϖA)_red, the ring A ×_{(A/ϖA)_red} B is integral perfectoid.
hypotheses: The map goes from B to (A/ϖ)_red, not conversely.
(A/ϖ)_red is a perfect F_p-algebra because A/p is semiperfect and ϖ | p.
proofSteps: (A/ϖ)_red is perfect, hence integral perfectoid (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, characteristic-p criterion), and A → (A/ϖ)_red is surjective.
Apply Q5/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-rings with A' = (A/ϖ)_red.
acceptance: For A = O_C, ϖ = p and B = F_p → k̄, the subring {x ∈ O_C : x mod m ∈ F_p} is integral perfectoid.
For B = (A/ϖ)_red with the identity the fibre product is A.

sources.match: Applies Proposition 2.1.4 to the surjection A ↠ (A/ϖ)_red and a perfect F_p-algebra mapping to it.

nodes.title: The relative tilting equivalence over an integral perfectoid ring
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid and ξ = (ξ_0, ξ_1, …) ∈ W(A^♭) a generator of ker θ_A. The functors A' ↦ A'^♭ and B ↦ W(B)/(ξ) are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between the category of integral perfectoid A-algebras and the category of perfect A^♭-algebras B that are classically ξ_0-adically complete. Under it θ_{A'} is the quotient map W(A'^♭) → W(A'^♭)/(ξ), and ξ generates ker θ_{A'} for every integral perfectoid A-algebra A'.
hypotheses: Morphisms are ring maps under A, respectively under A^♭.
ξ_1 is a unit of A^♭ and A^♭ is ξ_0-adically complete (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, generator criterion).
proofSteps: For a perfect ξ_0-adically complete A^♭-algebra B, W(B) is (p, [ξ_0])-adically complete, hence (p, ξ)-complete, and ξ stays distinguished because ξ_1 maps to a unit; so (W(B), (ξ)) is a perfect prism (PrismaticCohomology PR.0, distinguished elements and perfect prisms).

The equivalence between perfect prisms and integral perfectoid rings (PrismaticCohomology PR.0) gives that W(B)/(ξ) is integral perfectoid with tilt B; conversely for A' integral perfectoid over A, ξ maps to a generator of ker θ_{A'} (PerfectoidQuotients Q0) so A' = W(A'^♭)/(ξ).

The image of ξ generates ker θ_{A'}, so its zeroth coordinate generates the ideal (p^♭) of A'^♭ by Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms. Completeness for that ideal is therefore exactly ξ_0-adic completeness.
acceptance: For A an F_p-algebra (ξ = p, ξ_0 = 0) the equivalence is the identity on perfect A-algebras.
For A = O_C, perfectoid O_C-algebras correspond to perfect ξ_0-adically complete O_{C^♭}-algebras; O_C ↦ O_{C^♭}, O_C/(p^{1/p^∞}) ↦ k_C (the residue field of O_C).

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.9, first assertion, and first sentence of its proof, p. 14; equation (2.1.2.1), p. 10
sources.match: States the equivalence between perfectoid A-algebras and ξ_0-adically complete perfect A^♭-algebras via A' ↦ A'^♭ and B ↦ W(B)/(ξ), derived from the characterisation of perfectoid rings as W(B)/(ξ) with B perfect ξ_0-complete and ξ_1 a unit (Lau, Remark 8.6; Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 3.10).

nodes.title: Adic completeness transfers along tilting
nodes.statement: In the setting of Q6/relative-tilting-equivalence, let A' be an integral perfectoid A-algebra and ϖ^♭ ∈ A'^♭ an element dividing the image of ξ_0. Then A'^♭ is classically ϖ^♭-adically complete if and only if A' is classically ϖ-adically complete for ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯.
hypotheses: No torsion-freeness is assumed; the case ϖ^♭ = 0 is allowed (then ϖ = 0 and both sides hold trivially).
Completeness means classical completeness and separatedness.
proofSteps: Suppose A' is ϖ-adically complete. Since ϖ^♭ divides ξ_0, its sharp ϖ divides p up to a unit. Put b = (ϖ^♭)^{1/p}; then (b^♯)^p = ϖ divides p, and the b^♯-adic and ϖ-adic topologies agree. Apply Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms to b^♯ to obtain b-adic, hence ϖ^♭-adic, completeness of A'^♭.
Conversely W(A'^♭) is [ϖ^♭]-adically complete; it suffices that ξW(A'^♭) is closed for this topology (Stacks 031A), i.e. ξW ∩ [ϖ^♭]^nW = ξ([ϖ^♭]^nW) for all n.

Using the decomposition of the perfect ring A'^♭ along ϖ^♭ (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, torsion-free quotient) reduce to ϖ^♭ a nonzerodivisor and to n = 1. If ξw ∈ ([ϖ^♭]) with w = V^m(w_m, w_{m+1}, …) and w_m ∉ (ϖ^♭)^{p^m}, the Witt coordinates of ξw show (ϖ^♭)^{p^{m+1}} | w_m^p, hence (ϖ^♭)^{p^m} | w_m by perfectness, a contradiction.
acceptance: For A' = O_C and ϖ^♭ = (p^♭)^{1/p}, both rings are complete.
For a perfect F_p-algebra A' = A'^♭ the statement is a tautology.
For A' = ∏_{n∈ℕ} O_C and ϖ^♭ the constant sequence (p^♭)^{1/p}, both A' and A'^♭ = ∏_n O_{C^♭} are complete, although neither is noetherian.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.9, completeness assertion, and its proof, first paragraph, pp. 14–15
sources.match: States that A'^♭ is ϖ^♭-adically complete for ϖ^♭ | ξ_0 iff A' is ϖ-adically complete, proved by showing ξW(A'^♭) is [ϖ^♭]-adically closed via a Witt-coordinate computation (Bourbaki, AC IX §1 no. 6, Lemma 4) and Stacks 031A.
For an I-adically complete module M and a submodule K, M/K is I-adically complete exactly when K is closed, K = ∩(K + I^nM).

nodes.title: The tilt of a p-adically complete valuation ring
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring (a domain whose ideals are totally ordered) that is classically p-adically complete, with p a nonunit of V. Then V^♭ = PreTilt V p is a valuation ring; for x, y ∈ V^♭ one has x | y in V^♭ if and only if x^♯ | y^♯ in V; x^♯ = 0 only for x = 0; and x ↦ x^♯ induces an injective order-preserving homomorphism from the value group Frac(V^♭)^×/(V^♭)^× to Frac(V)^×/V^×.
hypotheses: No perfectoid hypothesis: the statement uses only the multiplicative description of the tilt.
If p = 0 in V, then V^♭ is the inverse-limit perfection lim_{Frob} V.
proofSteps: By Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid, V^♭ is multiplicatively the monoid of p-power compatible sequences (x_n) in V, with x^♯ = x_0.
If x^♯ = 0 then x_n^{p^n} = 0, so x = 0 since V is a domain; hence V^♭ is a nonzero ring without zero divisors.

If x^♯ | y^♯ with x ≠ 0, the valuation of V gives v(x_n) ≤ v(y_n) for each n, so z_n = y_n/x_n ∈ V form a compatible sequence with xz = y. Totality of the order on values gives the valuation-ring property and the value-group map.
acceptance: For V = O_C (C complete algebraically closed), V^♭ = O_{C^♭} is the valuation ring of the tilt, recovering Mathlib's PreTilt.isDomain in the rank-one valued-field case.
For V = Z_p, V^♭ = F_p is a field, a valuation ring with trivial value group, and the value-group map is not surjective.
For V a complete discrete valuation ring of characteristic p with residue field F_p, V^♭ = lim_{Frob} F_p⟦t⟧ = F_p is again a field: the tilt can lose the whole value group.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 2.1.9, second paragraph, first sentence, p. 15
sources.match: Shows that the tilt of a perfectoid valuation ring is a local domain in which of two elements one divides the other, using the multiplicative description (2.1.1.2); the argument given here needs only that description, not perfectoidness.

nodes.title: Tilting of perfectoid valuation rings
nodes.statement: Let A' be an integral perfectoid ring. Then A' is a valuation ring if and only if A'^♭ is a valuation ring. In that case every a ∈ A' is u·b^♯ with u ∈ A'^× and b ∈ A'^♭, and x ↦ x^♯ induces an order-preserving isomorphism of value groups Frac(A'^♭)^×/(A'^♭)^× ≅ Frac(A')^×/A'^×.
hypotheses: If pA' = 0 then A' = A'^♭ is perfect and the statement is trivial.
No rank assumption.
proofSteps: If A' is a valuation ring, A'^♭ is one by Q6/tilt-of-complete-valuation-ring.
If A'^♭ is a valuation ring, Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms and Q5/torsion-transfer show A' is local, p-torsion-free unless pA' = 0, and reduced (PerfectoidQuotients Q0).

Following Gabber–Ramero's argument: dividing by a power of (p^♭)^♯ one may assume a ∉ pA'; then a = b^♯ + (p^♭)^♯c with b ∉ (p^♭) by Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms, and b strictly divides p^♭, so a = b^♯(1 + (p^♭/b)^♯c) with the second factor a unit. This gives the valuation-ring property of A' and surjectivity of the value-group map, whose injectivity is Q6/tilt-of-complete-valuation-ring.
acceptance: O_C and O_{C^♭} correspond, with value groups both equal to |C^×| = |C^{♭×}|.
A product of two perfectoid valuation rings is not a valuation ring, and neither is its tilt, the product of the tilts.
The completion of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}] is a valuation ring whose tilt is the t-adic completion of F_p[t^{1/p^∞}], value group Z[1/p] on both sides.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.9, valuation-ring assertions, and proof, second paragraph, pp. 14–15
sources.match: States that A' is a valuation ring iff A'^♭ is, with value groups identified by ♯, and proves the converse by writing every element as a unit times a sharp, following Gabber–Ramero Proposition 16.5.50.

nodes.title: Localizations of complete valuation rings are complete
nodes.statement: Let V be a valuation ring, a ∈ V, and suppose V is classically a-adically complete. For every prime ideal 𝔮 ⊂ V containing a, the localization V_𝔮 is classically a-adically complete. Likewise, if V is complete for its valuation topology, so is V_𝔮 for every prime 𝔮.
hypotheses: a may be zero; then the statement is trivial.
proofSteps: Every element of V ∖ 𝔮 divides every element of 𝔮, so 𝔮 ≅ 𝔮V_𝔮 and 𝔮 kills V_𝔮/V.

In the inverse system of exact sequences 0 → V_𝔮/V → V/a^n → V_𝔮/a^n → V_𝔮/V → 0 the transition maps on the left copy are multiplication by a, hence zero; passing to the limit and using the snake lemma, a-adic completeness of V gives that of V_𝔮.
For the valuation topology, completeness of V is completeness of the nonunital ring 𝔮 with principal ideals open, which is unchanged by 𝔮 ≅ 𝔮V_𝔮.
acceptance: For V = O_C and 𝔮 = m the localization is V itself.
The prime 𝔮 = 0 is excluded when a ≠ 0: Frac(V) is not a-adically separated.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 2.1.9, last paragraph and footnote, p. 15
sources.match: Proves that for an a-adically complete valuation ring V and a prime 𝔮 ∋ a, V_𝔮 is a-adically complete, using 𝔮 ≅ 𝔮V_𝔮 and the inverse system of exact sequences; the footnote treats completeness for the valuation topology.

nodes.title: Localizations of perfectoid valuation rings
nodes.statement: Let V be an integral perfectoid valuation ring and 𝔮 ⊂ V a prime ideal, excluding 𝔮 = 0 when V has mixed characteristic (0, p). Then V_𝔮 is an integral perfectoid valuation ring. If V has mixed characteristic and dimension ≥ 1, its height-one prime 𝔭 = √(pV) satisfies (V_𝔭)^♭ ≅ (V^♭)_{𝔭^♭} with 𝔭^♭ = √(p^♭V^♭), and V_𝔭 is a rank-one perfectoid valuation ring, so V_𝔭[1/p] is a perfectoid field with ring of integers V_𝔭.
hypotheses: The excluded case: for mixed characteristic V, V_0 = Frac(V) is not p-adically complete.
proofSteps: On V and on V^♭ the p-adic, respectively p^♭-adic, topology is the valuation topology; Q6/valuation-ring-localization-completeness gives completeness of V_𝔮 and of (V^♭)_{𝔮^♭}.

Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms identifies V/p with V^♭/p^♭ compatibly with the localizations, so (V^♭)_{𝔮^♭} is a perfect complete valuation ring whose untilt by Q6/relative-tilting-equivalence is V_𝔮; Q6/tilting-valuation-rings identifies valuation rings on both sides.
For the height-one prime, V_𝔭 has rank one; a rank-one p-adically complete integral perfectoid valuation ring is the ring of integers of the perfectoid field V_𝔭[1/p] (PerfectoidSpaces P1.25).
acceptance: For V = O_C (rank one) the only allowed primes give V itself.
For a rank-two perfectoid valuation ring V with height-one prime 𝔭, V_𝔭 is the rank-one valuation ring through which V's coarsening factors.

sources.locator: proof of Proposition 2.1.9, third paragraph, p. 15, and Remark 2.1.10, p. 15
sources.match: Shows that the localization of a perfectoid valuation ring at its height-one prime is perfectoid with tilt the localization of the tilt, and remarks that every localization other than the zero-dimensional one in mixed characteristic is a perfectoid valuation ring.

nodes.title: Algebraically closed fraction fields under tilting
nodes.statement: Let A' be an integral perfectoid valuation ring. Then Frac(A') is algebraically closed if and only if Frac(A'^♭) is algebraically closed.
hypotheses: Dimension zero: an integral perfectoid field is a perfect field of characteristic p, and then A' = A'^♭.
proofSteps: If pA' = 0 then A' = A'^♭. Otherwise A' has mixed characteristic and dimension ≥ 1.
Frac(A') = Frac(A'_𝔭) for the height-one prime 𝔭, and by Q6/localizations-of-perfectoid-valuation-rings A'_𝔭[1/p] is a perfectoid field K whose tilt is Frac((A'^♭)_{𝔭^♭}) = Frac(A'^♭).
For a perfectoid field K, K is algebraically closed iff K^♭ is (PerfectoidSpaces P3.7(iii), Scholze Theorem 3.7(ii) and Proposition 3.8).
acceptance: For A' = O_C the statement is that C is algebraically closed iff C^♭ is.
For A' the completion of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}], neither Frac(A') nor Frac(A'^♭) = F_p((t^{1/p^∞}))^ is algebraically closed.

sources.locator: Proposition 2.1.9, parenthetical assertion, and proof, third paragraph, p. 15
sources.match: Asserts that A' has algebraically closed fraction field iff A'^♭ does, deduced for dimension ≤ 1 from Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, Theorem 3.7(ii) and in general by localizing at the height-one prime.
Tilting is an equivalence between finite extensions of a perfectoid field and of its tilt; a perfectoid field is algebraically closed iff its tilt is.

nodes.title: Perfectoid rings are quotients of torsion-free ones
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid and ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p such that A is classically ϖ-adically complete. (1) There are an integral perfectoid ring Ã, an element ϖ̃ ∈ Ã with ϖ̃^p | p such that Ã is ϖ̃-torsion-free and classically ϖ̃-adically complete, and a surjection Ã ↠ A carrying ϖ̃ to ϖ. (2) If ϖ has compatible p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ A, then Ã and ϖ̃ in (1) can be chosen so that ϖ̃ has compatible p-power roots ϖ̃^{1/p^n} ∈ Ã mapping to the ϖ^{1/p^n}. (3) Every integral perfectoid ring is a quotient of a p-torsion-free integral perfectoid ring.
hypotheses: Part (2) is the form used in the reduction step of the ind-syntomic André lemma (Q9); the source states only (1) and (3).
proofSteps: Write A = W(A^♭)/(ξ) with ξ_1 a unit and choose ϖ^♭ with ϖ = (ϖ^♭)^♯u, u ∈ A^× (Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms). In case (2) take ϖ^♭ = (ϖ^{1/p^n})_n ∈ A^♭ by Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid, so u = 1.

Let B_0 = F_p[X_a^{1/p^∞} : a ∈ A^♭] (perfection of a polynomial ring) with B_0 ↠ A^♭, X_a ↦ a; lift the ξ_i to ξ̃_i ∈ B_0 with X_{ϖ^♭}^p | ξ̃_0, and let B be the X_{ϖ^♭}-adic completion of B_0[1/ξ̃_1]: a perfect ξ̃_0-complete F_p-algebra surjecting onto A^♭.

The perfect F_p-algebra B is ξ̃_0-adically complete and ξ̃_1 is a unit, so the general Witt-quotient/perfect-prism criterion (PrismaticCohomology PR.0) makes Ã' = W(B)/(ξ̃) integral perfectoid; W(B) → W(A^♭) induces its surjection onto A; with ϖ̃' = (X_{ϖ^♭})^♯ one has ϖ̃'^p | p, Ã' is ϖ̃'-complete (Q6/tilting-completeness-transfer) and ϖ̃'-torsion-free (Q5/torsion-transfer, B being X_{ϖ^♭}-torsion-free).

In general replace Ã' by the ϖ̃'-adic completion Ã of Ã'[1/ũ] for a lift ũ of u, integral perfectoid by PerfectoidQuotients Q0 (completed étale extensions and sharp-ideal completions), and put ϖ̃ = ϖ̃'ũ. In case (2), u = 1: take Ã = Ã' and ϖ̃ = ϖ̃', whose roots ((X_{ϖ^♭})^{1/p^n})^♯ lift ϖ^{1/p^n}.
(3): take ξ̃_0 = X_{ξ_0}, replace X_{ϖ^♭} by X_{ξ_0}, and Ã = Ã'.
acceptance: For A = k̄ (perfect, ϖ = 0), Ã = the p-adic completion of W(k̄)[p^{1/p^∞}] with ϖ̃ = p^{1/p} works.
For A already ϖ-torsion-free, Ã = A works.
For A = F_p (perfect, p = 0), (3) is realised by the completion of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}] → F_p.

nodes.title: Stability of ind-fppf and ind-syntomic maps
nodes.statement: Ind-fppf maps and ind-syntomic maps are each stable under composition and base change. A nonempty finite product of ind-fppf A-algebras is ind-fppf; every finite product of ind-syntomic A-algebras is ind-syntomic, including the empty product. A filtered colimit of ind-fppf (resp. ind-syntomic) A-algebras is ind-fppf (resp. ind-syntomic). Moreover, A → A' is ind-fppf iff it is faithfully flat and A' is a filtered colimit of flat finitely presented A-algebras; a faithfully flat ind-syntomic map is ind-fppf.
hypotheses: All rings commutative; colimits filtered.
proofSteps: Factorization criteria (Stacks 07C3) reduce every assertion to finitely presented test algebras B → A'.

Composition: for A → A' → A'' and a test map B → A'', factor the induced A'-algebra map A' ⊗_A B → A'' through an A'-algebra S of the relevant finite-presentation class. Express A' as a filtered colimit of A-algebras of that class and descend S and the factorization to a sufficiently late stage. In the ind-fppf case descend faithful flatness of S by the finite-presentation limit theorem (EGA IV 11.2.6.1), then use transitivity of faithful flatness. In the ind-syntomic case descend syntomicity by Stacks 0C33 and use transitivity of syntomic maps; no faithful flatness is assumed in this case.

Base change, the finite products just specified and filtered colimits follow from the factorization criterion. Nonempty finite products preserve faithful flatness; the empty product is syntomic but is not faithfully flat over a nonzero base. Faithful flatness of the filtered colimits in question follows from flatness and nonvanishing fibres (Stacks 00HP).

If A → A' is faithfully flat and A' = colim S_j with S_j flat of finite presentation, a test map B → A' factors through some S_i, and Spec S_i → Spec A is surjective because Spec A' → Spec A factors through it; so S_i is faithfully flat. Syntomic algebras are flat of finite presentation, so faithfully flat ind-syntomic maps are ind-fppf.
acceptance: The composite A → A[T^{1/p^∞}] → A[T^{1/p^∞}, U^{1/p^∞}] is ind-syntomic and ind-fppf.
Base change of the ind-fppf map Z → Z[X] along Z → F_p gives F_p → F_p[X].

The ind-fppf product assertion is interpreted for nonempty finite products; the empty-product convention is recorded in source issue E5.

nodes.title: Glueing flatness along a nonzerodivisor
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring, f ∈ A and M an A-module. If f is a nonzerodivisor on A and on M, M[1/f] is flat over A[1/f], and M/fM is flat over A/fA, then M is flat over A. The same holds with flat replaced by faithfully flat.
hypotheses: No noetherian or finiteness hypothesis.
proofSteps: For an f-power-torsion A-module Q, Tor_i^A(M, Q) = 0 for i ≥ 1: for A/f-modules, M ⊗^L_A A/f = M/fM since f is regular on A and M, so Tor_i^A(M, Q) = Tor_i^{A/f}(M/fM, Q) = 0; extensions and filtered colimits give all f-power-torsion Q.
For an f-torsion-free Q, the sequence 0 → Q → Q[1/f] → C → 0 with C f-power torsion and Tor_1^A(M, Q[1/f]) = Tor_1^{A[1/f]}(M[1/f], Q[1/f]) = 0 give Tor_1^A(M, Q) = 0.
A general Q is an extension of Q/Q[f^∞] by Q[f^∞]. Faithful flatness: closed points of Spec A lie over V(f) or over D(f).
acceptance: For A = Z, f = p and M = Z_p: Z_p[1/p] = Q_p is torsion-free, hence flat, over Z[1/p], and Z_p/p = F_p is flat over F_p, so Z_p is flat over Z.
The hypothesis that f is a nonzerodivisor on M is needed: for M = Z/pZ over Z with f = p, M[1/p] = 0 and M/pM = F_p are flat, but M is not flat.

nodes.title: Affine blowup algebras along a regular pair
nodes.statement: Let R be a ring and a, g ∈ R such that a, g is an R-regular sequence (a is a nonzerodivisor on R and g is a nonzerodivisor on R/aR). Then the R-subalgebra R[g/a] of R[1/a] is isomorphic to R[X]/(aX − g), via X ↦ g/a.

proofSteps: The surjection R[X]/(aX − g) → R[g/a] exists since a·(g/a) = g.
Injectivity: a is a nonzerodivisor on R[X]/(aX − g) because a, g is regular; hence R[X]/(aX − g) embeds in its localization at a, which is R[1/a].

nodes.title: Continuous valuations for an element-adic topology
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring with the ϖ-adic topology for some ϖ ∈ A, and v a valuation on A with v(A) ≤ 1 and value group Γ_v. Then v is continuous (Tau Ceti's ValuationSpectrum.IsContinuous for the topological ring A) if and only if for every γ ∈ Γ_v there is n with v(ϖ)^n < γ. If moreover ϖ is a nonzerodivisor and A[1/ϖ] carries the topology in which A is an open subring with the ϖ-adic topology, a valuation w on A[1/ϖ] with w(A) ≤ 1 is continuous iff its restriction to A is.
hypotheses: Valuations are multiplicative with values in Γ ∪ {0}; v(ϖ) = 0 is allowed, and then v is continuous.
This fixes the convention of Česnavičius–Scholze §2.3 (continuity means that the powers of ϖ become smaller than every element of the value group) inside the Tau Ceti carrier.
proofSteps: If v(ϖ)^n < γ, then ϖ^nA ⊆ {a : v(a) < γ} because v(A) ≤ 1, so this additive subgroup is open; conversely openness of {v < γ} forces ϖ^nA ⊆ {v < γ} for some n.

For A[1/ϖ], A is open and its topology is ϖ-adic, so the same subgroups test continuity; Tau Ceti's description of continuous points of a Huber ring through an ideal of definition (Wedhorn Theorem 7.10) gives the same set.
acceptance: For A = Z_p and v the p-adic valuation, v is continuous.
The trivial valuation on Z_p (v(a) = 1 for a ≠ 0) is not continuous: v(p)^n = 1 is never below 1.
A valuation factoring through A/ϖ (so v(ϖ) = 0) is continuous.

nodes.title: The tilt of a continuous valuation
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid, ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p and A classically ϖ-adically complete, and ϖ^♭ ∈ A^♭ with (ϖ^♭)^♯ a unit multiple of ϖ. For a continuous valuation v on A (ϖ-adic topology) with v(A) ≤ 1, define v^♭ : A^♭ → Γ_v ∪ {0} by v^♭(x) = v(x^♯). Then v^♭ is a valuation on A^♭, continuous for the ϖ^♭-adic topology, with v^♭(A^♭) ≤ 1 and v^♭(ϖ^♭) = v(ϖ).
hypotheses: Continuity of v (Q8/adic-continuity-criterion) is used for the ultrametric inequality, through a ϖ-adic limit.
proofSteps: Multiplicativity, v^♭(0) = 0 and v^♭(1) = 1 hold because ♯ is a multiplicative map with 0^♯ = 0 and 1^♯ = 1 (Q5/tilt-inverse-limit-monoid).

Ultrametric inequality: (x + y)^♯ = lim_n ((x^{1/p^n})^♯ + (y^{1/p^n})^♯)^{p^n} in the ϖ-adic topology, because b^{p^{n−1}} mod p^n depends only on b mod p; each term has value ≤ max(v(x^♯), v(y^♯)), and continuity of v transfers the bound to the limit.
Continuity and v^♭(ϖ^♭) = v(ϖ) follow from (ϖ^♭)^♯ = unit·ϖ.
acceptance: For A = O_C and v its rank-one valuation, v^♭ is the valuation of O_{C^♭} defined by |x|_♭ = |x^♯| (PerfectoidSpaces P1, tilt of a perfectoid field).

nodes.title: The integral approximation lemma
nodes.statement: Let A be integral perfectoid and ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p such that A is classically ϖ-adically complete; let a ∈ A and m ≥ 0. There is a' ∈ A^♭ such that for every continuous valuation |·| on A with |A| ≤ 1, |a − a'^♯| ≤ |p|·max(|a'^♯|, |ϖ|^{pm}); in particular |a| ≤ |ϖ^{pm}| if and only if |a'^♯| ≤ |ϖ^{pm}|.
hypotheses: One may replace ϖ by an element whose p-th power is a unit multiple of p; this only enlarges the set of valuations and does not increase |ϖ|^p.
proofSteps: The second assertion follows from the first by the ultrametric inequality.

First replace ϖ by ρ with ρ^p a unit multiple of p, using Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms and a p-th root of p^♭ in the tilt. For each original continuous valuation, |ρ|^p = |p| ≤ |ϖ|^p, and it is also continuous for the ρ-adic topology. The bound proved with ρ therefore implies the requested bound with ϖ. In the remaining proof write ϖ for ρ.

Choose a generator ξ of ker θ with (ξ − [ξ̄])/p a unit of W(A^♭), ξ̄ = ξ mod p (Q5/sharp-quotient-isomorphisms), a lift z_0 ∈ W(A^♭) of a, and define z_{n+1} = [z̄_n] − [ξ̄]((ξ − [ξ̄])/p)^{−1}((z_n − [z̄_n])/p); put a' = z̄_m. Each z_n lifts a.

For the tilted valuation |·|_♭ of Q8/tilted-valuation, use the notation |z|_sup ≤ γ for the family of inequalities |z_{(j)}|_♭ ≤ γ for every j in the Teichmüller expansion z = Σ [z_{(j)}]p^j. Witt addition and multiplication preserve the corresponding ultrametric and product bounds. No maximum or supremum in the value group is assumed to exist.

Since ξ̄ is a unit multiple of (ϖ^♭)^p, |z_{n+1} − [z̄_n]|_sup ≤ |ϖ^♭|_♭^p|z_n|_sup; an induction on n, distinguishing whether |z̄_N|_♭ first exceeds |ϖ^♭|_♭^{p(N+1)} before or after m, gives |z_m − [z̄_m]|_sup ≤ max(|z̄_m|_♭, |ϖ^♭|_♭^{pm}), and θ(z_m − [z̄_m]) = a − a'^♯ gives the claim.
acceptance: For a = a''^♯ already a sharp, a' = a'' works with |a − a'^♯| = 0.
For m = 0 the bound is |a − a'^♯| ≤ |p| for every valuation, and a' = z̄_0 is any element of A^♭ whose sharp is congruent to a modulo p.

nodes.title: Topological nilpotence detected by continuous valuations
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring with the ϖ-adic topology for a nonzerodivisor ϖ ∈ A, and give A[1/ϖ] the topology for which A is an open subring with its ϖ-adic topology. An element a ∈ A[1/ϖ] is topologically nilpotent (a^n ∈ ϖA for all large n) if and only if |a| < 1 for every continuous valuation |·| on A[1/ϖ] with |A| ≤ 1. More generally the same holds for a Tate ring R, a ring of definition B ⊆ R and a ∈ R.
hypotheses: Ring of definition: open and bounded; the statement fails for open unbounded subrings (for R = Q_p and B = Q_p no continuous valuation is ≤ 1 on B).
proofSteps: If a^n ∈ ϖA then |a|^n ≤ |ϖ| < 1.
Conversely |a| ≤ 1 for all such valuations makes a integral over A (Wedhorn Proposition 7.18(1), Tau Ceti isIntegral_of_forall_continuous_valuation_le_one), so {a^i} is bounded.
If A^{∘∘}·A[1/a] = A[1/a] then a satisfies a^N + Σ a_i a^i = 0 with a_i topologically nilpotent, so a is topologically nilpotent.

Otherwise choose a maximal ideal 𝔪 ⊇ A^{∘∘}A[1/a] of A[1/a], a minimal prime 𝔭 ⊆ 𝔪 extending to a minimal prime of A[1/ϖ][1/a] (Stacks 00E0, 00FK), a valuation ring V dominating (A[1/a]/𝔭)_𝔪 (Stacks 00IA), and V̄ = V/∩ϖ^nV: the induced valuation on A[1/ϖ] is continuous, ≤ 1 on A and has |1/a| ≤ 1, contradicting |a| < 1.
acceptance: For A = Z_p, a = p/1 is topologically nilpotent and |p| < 1 for every continuous valuation.
For A = Z_p, a = 1 has |1| = 1 and is not topologically nilpotent.
For A = Z_p⟨T⟩ and a = T, the Gauss valuation has |T| = 1, so T is not topologically nilpotent.

sources.match: States that a ∈ A[1/ϖ] is topologically nilpotent iff |a| < 1 for all continuous valuations with |A| ≤ 1, a special case of Gabber–Ramero Corollary 15.4.27(ii), proved via Huber's Lemma 3.3(i) and a dominating valuation ring.

For an f-adic ring, open integrally closed subrings correspond to sets of continuous valuations; in particular an element bounded by 1 by all continuous valuations bounded by 1 on an open subring is integral over it.

nodes.title: The root extension of a set of monic polynomials
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring and ϖ ∈ A a nonzerodivisor with ϖ^p | p admitting compatible p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ A, and let 𝒫 be a set of monic polynomials of positive degree in A[T]. Put A_0 = A[T_P^{1/p^n} : P ∈ 𝒫, n ≥ 0], the polynomial algebra on compatible p-power roots of one variable T_P for each P; A_∞ = A_0[P(T_P)/ϖ^m : P ∈ 𝒫, m ≥ 0] ⊆ A_0[1/ϖ] and I_∞ ⊆ A_∞ the ideal generated by the P(T_P)/ϖ^m; A' = the p-integral closure of A_∞ in A_∞[1/ϖ] = A_0[1/ϖ] (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, p-integral closure), and I' ⊆ A' the ideal generated by the P(T_P)/ϖ^m. Then I_∞ and I' are ϖ-divisible, A_∞/I_∞ = A_0/(P(T_P) : P ∈ 𝒫) inside its localization at ϖ, A'/I' is ϖ-torsion-free and is the p-integral closure of A_∞/I_∞ in (A_∞/I_∞)[1/ϖ], A'/I' is integral over A, (A'/I')[1/ϖ] is a filtered colimit of finite free A[1/ϖ]-algebras, and the class α_P of T_P in A'/I' is a root of P with compatible p-power roots, the classes of T_P^{1/p^n}.
hypotheses: Positive degree is essential: for P = 1 one gets 1/ϖ^m ∈ A_∞, so I' is the unit ideal and A'/I' = 0.
No completeness and no perfectoid hypothesis is needed for the construction; Q9/ind-syntomic-andre-lemma adds them.
proofSteps: A_∞[1/ϖ] = A_0[1/ϖ] since the adjoined elements lie there; I_∞ is ϖ-divisible because P(T_P)/ϖ^m = ϖ·P(T_P)/ϖ^{m+1}.

Each P is monic, so A_0/(P(T_P))_P embeds in its localization at ϖ (ϖ, P(T_P) is regular), and every element of that subring lifts to A_0; hence A_∞/I_∞ = A_0/(P(T_P))_P, which is integral over A with (A_∞/I_∞)[1/ϖ] ind-finite-free over A[1/ϖ].

ϖ-divisibility of I' and the injectivity criterion of PerfectoidQuotients Q0 (p-integral closedness through Frobenius modulo ϖ) identify A'/I' with the p-integral closure of A_∞/I_∞; p-integral closures are integral (PerfectoidQuotients Q0).
acceptance: For 𝒫 = ∅, A' is the p-integral closure of A in A[1/ϖ] and I' = 0.

sources.locator: proof of Theorem 2.3.4 (§2.3.6), first and second paragraphs, pp. 25–26
sources.match: Defines A_∞, its ϖ-divisible ideal I_∞, the p-integral closure A' and I', shows that the class of T_P is a root with compatible roots, that A'/I' is integral over A, ind-finite-free after inverting ϖ, and the p-integral closure of A_∞/I_∞ = A[T_P^{1/p^n}]/(P(T_P)).

nodes.title: The p-integral closure for one polynomial
nodes.statement: Let A be ϖ-Henselian, with ϖ ∈ A a nonzerodivisor, ϖ^p | p, admitting compatible p-power roots, and with integral perfectoid ϖ-adic completion. Let P ∈ A[T] be monic of positive degree, m > 0, A_0 = A[T^{1/p^∞}] and A'_m the p-integral closure of A_0[P/ϖ^m] in A_0[1/ϖ]. Then there are t ≥ 0 and q_j ∈ A_0 (j ≥ 0) such that: ϖ^{m/p^j}, q_j is an A_0-regular sequence; q_{j+1}^p ≡ q_j mod ϖ^{mp}A_0; the image of q_j in (A/ϖ^{1/p^{j+t}})[T^{1/p^n}] is monic for large n; the subalgebras A_0[q_j/ϖ^{m/p^j}] ≅ A_0[X_j]/(ϖ^{m/p^j}X_j − q_j) increase with j; and A'_m is their union. Consequently A'_m is ind-syntomic over A.
hypotheses: An element of B[T^{1/p^∞}] is monic of degree d ∈ Z[1/p]_{≥0} if it is T^d plus a B-linear combination of T^e with e < d.
ϖ^{m/p^j} denotes (ϖ^{1/p^j})^m.
proofSteps: Â_0, the ϖ-adic completion of A_0, is integral perfectoid (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, completed root polynomials). By Q8/integral-approximation-lemma there is Q ∈ Â_0 with compatible roots Q^{1/p^j} and |P − Q| < max(|Q|, |ϖ^m|) for every continuous valuation on Â_0[1/ϖ] with |Â_0| ≤ 1.

Then {|P/ϖ^m| ≤ 1} = {|Q/ϖ^m| ≤ 1} in Spa(Â_0[1/ϖ], Â_0^+), the continuous valuations of Â_0[P/ϖ^m] and Â_0[Q/ϖ^m] coincide, and by Q8/topological-nilpotence-criterion a power of P/ϖ^m − Q/ϖ^m lies in ϖ times either algebra; also P − Q ∈ ϖ^{1/p^t}Â_0 for some t by the iterated Frobenius bijections modulo ϖ^{1/p^n} (PerfectoidSpaces P1.24).

So Q^{1/p^j} is monic modulo ϖ^{1/p^{j+t}}, ϖ^{m/p^j}, Q^{1/p^j} is regular (Stacks 07DV), Â_0[Q^{1/p^j}/ϖ^{m/p^j}] ≅ Â_0[X^{1/p^j}]/(ϖ^{m/p^j}X^{1/p^j} − Q^{1/p^j}) (Q7/regular-blowup-algebra), and the union over j has perfectoid completion, hence is p-integrally closed; it is the p-integral closure of both Â_0[P/ϖ^m] and Â_0[Q/ϖ^m].

Descend to A_0: choose d with (P − Q)^{p^d} ∈ ϖ^{mp^d} in both completed algebras, q ≡ Q mod ϖ^{mp^d} in A_0 and q_j ≡ Q^{1/p^j} mod ϖ^{mp}; the completions of A_0[P/ϖ^m] and A_0[q/ϖ^m] agree, so their p-integral closures agree, and the union of the A_0[q_j/ϖ^{m/p^j}] is p-integrally closed because modulo ϖ it is the completed perfectoid one.

Ind-syntomicity: each A[T^{1/p^n}][X_j]/(ϖ^{m/p^j}X_j − q_j) is syntomic over A by Q7/fibrewise-hypersurface-syntomic (the element is linear in X_j where ϖ is invertible and monic in T^{1/p^n} where it is not), and filtered colimits of ind-syntomic algebras are ind-syntomic (Q7/ind-maps-stability).
acceptance: For P = T one may take Q = T, t = 0 and q_j = T^{1/p^j}: A'_m = ∪_j A_0[T^{1/p^j}/ϖ^{m/p^j}], each stage A_0[X_j]/(ϖ^{m/p^j}X_j − T^{1/p^j}) being syntomic over A.
The union is needed: for P = T and m = 1, T^{1/p}/ϖ^{1/p} is p-integral over A_0[T/ϖ] (its p-th power is T/ϖ) but is not in A_0[T/ϖ], whose elements have integral T^{1/p}-coefficient.

sources.match: Reduces ind-syntomicity to one monic P and m > 0, approximates P by Q with compatible roots via Lemma 2.3.1, compares rational subsets and uses Lemma 2.3.2, describes the p-integral closure as the union of A_0[q_j/ϖ^{m/p^j}] and concludes with Stacks 00SW.

nodes.title: The ind-syntomic André lemma
nodes.statement: Let A be a ring and ϖ ∈ A with ϖ^p | p admitting compatible p-power roots ϖ^{1/p^n} ∈ A, and suppose either (i) A is integral perfectoid and classically ϖ-adically complete, or (ii) A is ϖ-Henselian, ϖ is a nonzerodivisor of A, and the ϖ-adic completion of A is integral perfectoid. Then there are a faithfully flat, ind-syntomic, ϖ-Henselian A-algebra A' whose ϖ-adic completion Â' is integral perfectoid, and a ϖ-divisible ideal I' ⊆ A' with A'/I' faithfully flat over A, such that every monic polynomial P ∈ A'[T] of positive degree has a root α_P ∈ A'/I' admitting compatible p-power roots α_P^{1/p^n} ∈ A'/I'; in particular these roots exist in Â' ≅ (A'/I')^.
hypotheses: ϖ-Henselian means that (A, ϖA) is a henselian pair; Henselizations of pairs are those of SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.12.
Monic means monic of positive degree: the constant 1 has no root in a nonzero ring (recorded as a source issue).
proofSteps: Reduce (i) to (ii): by Q6/torsion-free-perfectoid-presentation (2), A is a quotient of a ϖ̃-torsion-free, ϖ̃-complete integral perfectoid Ã with ϖ̃ having compatible roots lifting those of ϖ; a solution (Ã', Ĩ') for Ã gives A' = Ã' ⊗_Ã A with the image of Ĩ' (completed tensor products, PerfectoidQuotients Q0).

In case (ii) it suffices to treat monic P ∈ A[T]: iterating countably many times, A'_∞ = colim A'_n with I'_∞ = Σ I'_iA'_∞ works for all monic polynomials over A'_∞, since each A'_n/ΣI'_i is faithfully flat over the previous one. ϖ-Henselianity is restored at the end by ϖ-Henselization, which is ind-étale and faithfully flat because ϖ lies in every maximal ideal (SchemeAndStackFoundations §§0.12–0.13; Stacks 00HP).

For 𝒫 the monic polynomials over A take A', I' of Q9/andre-root-extension. Its ϖ-adic completion is integral perfectoid by PerfectoidQuotients Q0 (perfectoid completion of p-integral closures), as every element of A_∞/ϖ^p is a p-th power.
A'/I' is integral over A and ϖ-torsion-free with ind-finite-free localization, so Spec(A'/I') → Spec A is surjective, and A'/I' is A-flat by Q7/flatness-glueing once (A'/I')/ϖ ≅ A'/ϖ is A/ϖ-flat.
Ind-syntomicity of A' over A (hence flatness of A'/ϖ) reduces by filtered colimits to finitely many, then one, monic P and to the p-integral closures A'_m of Q9/single-polynomial-p-integral-closure.
acceptance: For A = O_C (C complete algebraically closed) and ϖ = p^{1/p}, A' = A and I' = 0 satisfy the conclusion: O_C is complete, absolutely integrally closed, and every element has compatible p-power roots.

For p odd, A the p-adic completion of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}] (residue field F_p), ϖ = p^{1/p} and P = T² − u with u ∈ Z_p^× not a square, P has no root in A, while A'/I' contains a root of P with compatible p-power roots.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.3.4, p. 25, and its proof (§2.3.6), pp. 25–28
sources.match: States the ind-syntomic André lemma under hypotheses (i) or (ii) and proves it following Gabber–Ramero Theorem 16.9.17, reducing (i) to (ii) by Proposition 2.1.12, iterating countably, Henselizing, and verifying flatness by glueing and ind-syntomicity one polynomial at a time.

nodes.title: Consequences of the ind-syntomic André lemma
nodes.statement: In the situation of Q9/ind-syntomic-andre-lemma: the integral perfectoid ring Â' contains compatible p-power roots of every element of A, and Â'/ϖ is faithfully flat over A/ϖ. In particular A → Â' is a ϖ-completely faithfully flat map to an integral perfectoid ring in which every element of A has compatible p-power roots, which recovers André's lemma in the form of Bhatt, On the direct summand conjecture, Theorem 1.5, with faithful flatness in place of almost faithful flatness modulo ϖ.
hypotheses: Â' ≅ (A'/I')^ because I' is ϖ-divisible.
proofSteps: Apply Q9/ind-syntomic-andre-lemma to the polynomials T − a, a ∈ A; their roots and the compatible roots of those roots lie in A'/I', hence in Â'.
Â'/ϖ = A'/ϖ = (A'/I')/ϖ is faithfully flat over A/ϖ, A'/I' being faithfully flat over A.
acceptance: For A a perfect F_p-algebra and ϖ = 0, every element of A has unique compatible p-power roots, Â' = A' and the assertion is faithful flatness of A' over A.

nodes.title: p-Zariski rings and p-Zariskization
nodes.statement: A ring A is p-Zariski if 1 + pA ⊆ A^×, equivalently if p lies in the Jacobson radical of A (in every maximal ideal). The p-Zariskization of a ring B is the localization B_{1+pB} of B at the multiplicative set 1 + pB.
hypotheses: p is a fixed prime; the zero ring is p-Zariski.
proofSteps: 1 + pB is multiplicatively closed: (1 + pb)(1 + pc) = 1 + p(b + c + pbc).
The equivalence with the Jacobson radical is the characterisation of the Jacobson radical by units of 1 + xA.
acceptance: A p-adically complete ring is p-Zariski.

nodes.title: Semiperfectoid covers of p-Zariski rings
nodes.statement: Every p-Zariski ring A admits a faithfully flat map A → A_∞ such that: the p-adic completion of the reduced ring A_∞^red is integral perfectoid; A_∞ is a quotient of a p-torsion-free, p-Henselian ring Ã_∞ whose p-adic completion is integral perfectoid; and every monic polynomial of positive degree over Ã_∞ has a root in Ã_∞, hence also over A_∞ and over A_∞^red.
hypotheses: Monic polynomials of positive degree; A = 0 is allowed with A_∞ = 0.
proofSteps: Replace A by the p-Zariskization of the countable iteration of A ↦ A[X_a^{1/p^∞} : a ∈ A]/(X_a − a : a ∈ A); this is faithfully flat (each step is free, and p-Zariskization preserves faithful flatness over p-Zariski rings), and now every a ∈ A has compatible p-power roots.

Such A is a quotient of the p-torsion-free Z_(p)-algebra Ã, the p-Zariskization of Z[p^{1/p^∞}][X_a^{1/p^∞} : a ∈ A], whose p-adic completion is integral perfectoid (PerfectoidQuotients Q0, completed root polynomials).

Apply Q9/ind-syntomic-andre-lemma (ii) to the p-Henselization Ã^h of Ã, with ϖ = p^{1/p}. Write its output as B with ideal J, and take Ã_∞ = C = B/J: it is C that has roots of all positive-degree monic polynomials, by lifting their coefficients to B. The map Ã^h → C is faithfully flat, so C is p-torsion-free; it is p-Henselian as a quotient of B, and J being ϖ-divisible gives the same p-adic completion as B, hence an integral perfectoid completion. The map Ã → Ã^h is faithfully flat because Ã is p-Zariski. Put A_∞ = C ⊗_Ã A; this is a quotient of C since A is a quotient of Ã.

A_∞ is faithfully flat over A. nodes.title: Towers over complete regular local rings
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a complete regular local ring with residue field k. (a) There is a filtered direct system (R_i, 𝔪_i)_{i∈I} of regular local finite flat R-algebras with 𝔪_i = 𝔪R_i, each unramified if R is unramified (mixed characteristic (0, p) with p ∉ 𝔪²), whose colimit (colim R_i, colim 𝔪_i) is a regular local ring with residue field an algebraic closure k̄ of k. (b) If R has mixed characteristic (0, p) and k is perfect, write R ≅ W(k)⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧/(p − f) with f = x_1 (R unramified) or f ∈ (p, x_1, …, x_d)² (R ramified). Then R_n = W(k)⟦x_1^{1/p^n}, …, x_d^{1/p^n}⟧/(p − f) are regular local finite flat R-algebras of p-power rank, R_∞ = colim_n R_n = W(k)⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧/(p − f) (colimit, not completed), and the p-adic completion of R_∞ is integral perfectoid.
hypotheses: Unramified is the convention of Česnavičius–Scholze §1.4: mixed characteristic (0, p) and p ∉ 𝔪².
The bracket ⟦x^{1/p^∞}⟧ denotes the colimit of the power series rings in x^{1/p^m}, without a further (x)-adic completion.
proofSteps: (a) is PerfectoidSpaces P7.16a (Česnavičius, Purity for the Brauer group, Lemma 5.1): its stages are W_i⟦x⟧ or W_i⟦x⟧/(p − f) with W_i complete discrete valuation rings with uniformizer p, so they are unramified exactly when R is.

(b) is PerfectoidSpaces P7.17 (Česnavičius, Lemma 5.2) in a uniform presentation: for f = x_1, W(k)⟦x⟧/(p − x_1) ≅ W(k)⟦x_2, …, x_d⟧ and R_n ≅ W(k)[p^{1/p^n}]⟦x_2^{1/p^n}, …, x_d^{1/p^n}⟧, which is P7.17's unramified tower; for f ∈ (p, x)² the towers agree literally.
acceptance: For R = Z_p (d = 1, f = x_1): R_n = Z_p[p^{1/p^n}] and the completion of R_∞ is that of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}].
For R = Z_p⟦x⟧/(p − x²) = Z_p[√p] (ramified, p ∈ 𝔪²): R_n = Z_p⟦x^{1/p^n}⟧/(p − x²).
For R = F_p⟦x⟧ in (a) the stages are F_{p^n}⟦x⟧ and the colimit is not complete.

nodes.title: Perfectoid covers of complete regular local rings via prisms
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete noetherian regular local ring of dimension d and mixed characteristic (0, p) with residue field k (not necessarily perfect). Choose a Cohen ring W for k with a Frobenius lift φ_W and write R = A/(f) with A = W⟦x_1, …, x_d⟧ and f ∈ 𝔪_A ∖ 𝔪_A² (Cohen structure theorem). Then A carries a δ-structure extending φ_W with φ(x_i) = x_i^p for which f is distinguished (after a change of variables when f ∈ (x_1, …, x_d) + 𝔪_A²), (A, (f)) is a prism, its perfection (A_∞, (f)) is a perfect prism, R_∞ = A_∞/(f) is integral perfectoid, and R → R_∞ is faithfully flat.
hypotheses: The decomposition of f in 𝔪_A/𝔪_A² as a_0p + Σa_ix_i distinguishes the cases a_0 ≠ 0 and a_0 = 0; in the second, change variables to f = x_1 − p.
Faithful flatness is ordinary faithful flatness, obtained from p-complete faithful flatness because R is noetherian.
proofSteps: If a_0 ≠ 0, evaluation at x = 0 is a δ-map A → W with topologically nilpotent kernel carrying f to an element of p-adic valuation one, so f is distinguished (PrismaticCohomology PR.0, distinguished elements and rigidity); if a_0 = 0, after the change of variables f = x_1 − p and the same δ-structure, f is distinguished.

A is p-torsion-free and A/p = k⟦x⟧ is regular, so φ_A is p-completely faithfully flat (Kunz, EnhancedDerivedSheaves §E1.6); the perfection of the prism is a p-completely faithfully flat map of prisms with perfect target (PrismaticCohomology PR.0, perfection of a prism).

R_∞ = A_∞/(f) is integral perfectoid by the perfect-prism equivalence, and R → R_∞ is p-completely faithfully flat. Since p is a nonzerodivisor on R, derived p-complete flatness gives Tor_1^R(R_∞, R/p) = R_∞[p] = 0. Both rings are classically p-complete (for R use its noetherian maximal-ideal completeness and p ∈ 𝔪). The noetherian-base criterion of DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1 now gives ordinary flatness, and nonzero closed fibre gives faithful flatness.
acceptance: For R = Z_p (d = 1): A = Z_p⟦x_1⟧ and f = p − x_1 has a_0 ≠ 0; the perfection is the completed Z_p⟦x_1^{1/p^∞}⟧ and R_∞ is the p-adic completion of Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}].
The presentation must use d = dim R variables: writing Z_p = W(F_p)/(p) instead would give the crystalline prism (Z_p, (p)), whose perfection has reduction F_p, which is not faithfully flat over Z_p.
For R = W(k)⟦x⟧ with k perfect and f = x_1 − p, R_∞ is the p-adic completion of the tower of Q10/regular-local-towers (b).

nodes.title: The completed absolute integral closure is perfectoid
nodes.statement: Let R be a domain whose fraction field K has characteristic 0, with p a nonunit of R, and let R⁺ be the integral closure of R in an algebraic closure of K. Then R⁺ is p-torsion-free and absolutely integrally closed, and its p-adic completion (R⁺)^∧ is integral perfectoid; every element of R⁺ has compatible p-power roots in R⁺.
hypotheses: R need not be noetherian or complete.
p is a nonunit of R⁺ because R → R⁺ is integral.
proofSteps: R⁺ is a domain of characteristic 0, hence p-torsion-free; it is integrally closed in its fraction field, which is algebraically closed, so every monic polynomial of positive degree over R⁺ has a root in R⁺; in particular p^{1/p} ∈ R⁺, Frobenius of R⁺/p is surjective, and compatible p-power roots exist by choosing roots successively.

With π = p^{1/p}, (π^p) = (p) and R⁺ is integrally closed in R⁺[1/p], so the p-adic completion is integral perfectoid by PerfectoidQuotients Q0 (p-integral closedness criterion, ordinary integral closedness form).
acceptance: For R = Z_p, R⁺ = Z̄_p and (R⁺)^∧ = O_{C_p}.
Characteristic 0 is needed for p^{1/p} to separate p-adic and characteristic-p behaviour: for R = F_p⟦t⟧, R⁺ is a perfect ring and p = 0, so (R⁺)^∧ = R⁺ is perfect.

sources.match: Uses that the p-adic completion of R⁺ is perfectoid to obtain the map T_perfd → R⁺/p^n from the universal property of perfectoidization.
For a p-torsion-free ring with (π^p) = (p), integral closedness in its p-inverted ring and surjective Frobenius modulo p make its p-adic completion perfectoid.

nodes.title: A perfectoid cover inside the completed absolute integral closure
nodes.statement: Let (R, 𝔪) be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p) with perfect residue field k, and R⁺ an absolute integral closure. The tower R_n of Q10/regular-local-towers (b) embeds R-linearly into R⁺ by choosing compatible roots of the x_i in R⁺; with R_∞ = colim R_n ⊆ R⁺, the map R → R̂_∞ to the p-adic completion is faithfully flat, R̂_∞ is integral perfectoid, and R̂_∞ → (R⁺)^∧ is an injective R-algebra map.
hypotheses: Choices: compatible systems x_i^{1/p^n} ∈ R⁺ (Q10/absolute-integral-closure-completion); for f = x_1 the roots of x_1 are roots of p.
proofSteps: Each R_n is a domain finite over R, so it embeds in R⁺ once the roots of the x_i are chosen compatibly; the embeddings are compatible in n.

R → R_n is finite free (finite flat over a local ring), so R → R_∞ is faithfully flat and R/p → R_∞/p = R̂_∞/p is faithfully flat; R and R̂_∞ are p-torsion-free and p-complete, so R → R̂_∞ is faithfully flat (DerivedDeRhamCohomology DD.1, Bhatt's criterion).
R_∞ is integrally closed (a filtered union of regular, hence normal, domains), so R_∞ ∩ pR⁺ = pR_∞ and the completed map is injective.
acceptance: For R = Z_p: R_∞ = Z_p[p^{1/p^∞}] ⊆ Z̄_p and R̂_∞ ⊆ O_{C_p}.
For imperfect k the explicit tower does not apply; Q10/prismatic-cover-of-regular-local-ring gives a faithfully flat perfectoid cover, but no map to (R⁺)^∧ is constructed here (recorded gap).

nodes.title: Almost vanishing of Tor along finite subextensions of R⁺
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete regular local ring of mixed characteristic (0, p), R⁺ an absolute integral closure, S ⊆ R⁺ a finite R-subalgebra, n > 0, and c ∈ pR nonzero with R[1/c] → S[1/c] finite étale. Suppose given a faithfully flat map R → R_∞ to an integral perfectoid ring together with an R-algebra map R_∞ → (R⁺)^∧. Then for every i > 0 and every R/p^n-module N, the image of Tor_i^{R/p^n}(S/p^n, N) → Tor_i^{R/p^n}(R⁺/p^n, N) is annihilated by c^{1/p^k} for every k ≥ 0 (for any compatible system of p-power roots of c in R⁺). When the residue field of R is perfect, the hypothesis on R_∞ is satisfied by Q10/perfectoid-cover-inside-plus-closure.
hypotheses: Such c exists: S is generically étale over R since Frac(R) has characteristic 0, and multiplying a nonzero element by p keeps the étale locus.
c-almost zero means annihilated by all c^{1/p^k}; it is the J_perfd-almost zero condition for J = (c) after mapping to R⁺, where c has compatible roots.
proofSteps: T = S ⊗_R R_∞ is a finitely presented finite R_∞-algebra, finite étale after inverting c. By Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 10.9 (PrismaticCohomology Part I, integral perfectoidization and arbitrary-ideal almost purity), T_perfd is integral perfectoid and R_∞/p^n → T_perfd/p^n is almost finite projective for the almost setting attached to J = (c).

As R/p^n → R_∞/p^n is flat, Tor_i^{R/p^n}(T_perfd/p^n, N) = Tor_i^{R_∞/p^n}(T_perfd/p^n, R_∞ ⊗_R N), which is c-almost zero for i > 0; here c ∈ pR and the p-torsion of T_perfd, killed by all p^{1/p^k} (Q5/torsion-transfer), is c-almost zero.

S/p^n → R⁺/p^n factors as S/p^n → T/p^n → T_perfd/p^n → R⁺/p^n, the last map by the universal property of T → T_perfd (Bhatt–Scholze Theorem 10.11) applied to T → (R⁺)^∧, which is integral perfectoid (Q10/absolute-integral-closure-completion). The middle Tor group being c-almost zero gives the claim.
acceptance: If S = R the map is from Tor_i^{R/p^n}(R/p^n, N) = 0 for i > 0, and the statement is empty.
If R → S is finite étale, S/p^n is flat over R/p^n, the source Tor groups vanish for i > 0, and any c ∈ pR works.
